_about: Defect classes for this repository, read by projectos.infrastructure.defect_sweep. Declarations (name, source, instances, enforcement_test) are founder-owned and hand-written; the sweep only ever adds an observed 'last_sweep' block. A class is closed when its enforcement test makes a NEW instance fail the build.

DC-1.name: A value believed rather than observed
DC-1.description: A claim accepted because something reported it, rather than because it was read from the thing itself. The general form of every trust-the-report defect: an exit code trusted instead of a parsed summary, a seat tag trusted instead of a repo root, a clock trusted instead of an anchored instant.
DC-1.source: TradeOS observed-fact rule (DC-1); extended to fleet time by assignment FLEET-CLOCK, 2026-08-14

instances.what: `TZ='Asia/Kolkata' date` returned GMT with no tzdata present and no error, putting reported times 5.5 hours out.
instances.why_it_is_this_class: A timezone was requested and the answer believed; the offset was never checked against anything.
instances.now_caught_by: now_ist() converts by a fixed +05:30 offset and never depends on a named-zone lookup; tzdata is consulted only as a cross-check that raises on disagreement.

instances.what: Chat stamped filenames from an assumed time rather than a read one on at least three occasions. MAGNITUDE UNKNOWN.
instances.why_magnitude_is_unverified: A 64-minute figure was originally attributed to Chat's clock error, reported by COWORK against the local mirror's mtime. Measurement (PROJECTOS, 2026-08-14) showed that for a Drive-synced file the local mtime is the SYNC write, not the authoring moment, so that figure is part clock error and part sync latency and the two are not separable from a seat. Chat amended its own entry rather than let the number stand: being wrong about the size of your own error is still being wrong. The occurrences are real; only the magnitude is unknown.
instances.why_it_is_this_class: The time was supplied from belief rather than read. It sorts, so it corrupts 'oldest file first' ordering silently.
instances.now_caught_by: stamp_for_filename() is the single way to produce a stamp and raises rather than returning a plausible time when the clock cannot be established. Magnitude for synced files is measurable only against Drive's server-side timestamp, which is the Chat-owned half of the split check.

DC-1.tolerance: DECLARED by the founder on 2026-08-14 at 120s on the resolution argument — see docs/parameter_registry.json (FLEET-CLOCK-SKEW-TOLERANCE). Code still has no default: it resolves the value and fails closed when absent.
DC-1.check_ownership: Split by anchor, ruled 2026-08-14. Locally-written files: PROJECTOS, via check_local_file against local mtime (the authoring moment here). Synced files: CHAT, against Drive's server-side createdTime/modifiedTime — this seat cannot see that fact and refuses the check rather than measuring sync latency and calling it clock error.
